t: Section 93 of title 14, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsections:“(c) Marine Safety Responsibilities.—In exercising the Commandant’s duties and responsibilities with regard to marine safety, the individual with the highest rank who meets the experience qualifications set forth in section 50(a)(3) shall serve as the principal advisor to the Commandant regarding—“(1) the operation, regulation, inspection, identification, manning, and measurement of vessels, including plan approval and the application of load lines;“(2) approval of materials, equipment, appliances, and associated equipment;“(3) the reporting and investigation of marine casualties and accidents;“(4) the licensing, certification, documentation, protection and relief of merchant seamen;“(5) suspension and revocation of licenses and certificates;“(6) enforcement of manning requirements, citizenship requirements, control of log books;“(7) documentation and numbering of vessels;“(8) State boating safety programs;“(9) commercial instruments and maritime liens;“(10) the administration of bridge safety;“(11) administration of the navigation rules;“(12) the prevention of pollution from vessels;“(13) ports and waterways safety;“(14) waterways management; including regulation for regattas and marine parades;“(15) aids to navigation; and“(16) other duties and powers of the Secretary related to marine safety and stewardship.“(d) Other Authority Not Affected.—Nothing in subsection (c) affects—“(1) the authority of Coast Guard officers and members to enforce marine safety regulations using authority under section 89 of this title; or“(2) the exercise of authority under section 91 of this title and the provisions of law codified at sections 191 through 195 of title 50 on the date of enactment of this paragraph.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "principal advisor" role, plus references to "regulation" and "State boating safety programs", signals advisory participation or rulemaking. But the advisor is a Coast Guard officer inside the federal government, and the listed items are only subject areas of internal advice. The section grants no rulemaking authority and requires no consultation with states, the public, or any other outside party.
fable.s: the individual with the highest rank who meets the experience qualifications set forth in section 50(a)(3) shall serve as the principal advisor to the Commandant

opus.w: The only advisory relationship here is between a Coast Guard officer and the Commandant, so both sides are inside the federal government and this is not participation. References to 'regulation' and 'State boating safety programs' are just subjects of that internal advice. They do not give the Coast Guard new rulemaking authority, and they do not require consulting states or anyone else outside the government. Nothing in the section gives outside parties a role in, or a right to challenge, a federal decision.
opus.s: the individual with the highest rank who meets the experience qualifications set forth in section 50(a)(3) shall serve as the principal advisor to the Commandant regarding

This is an internal organizational structure within the federal government. The mention of 'State boating safety programs' is a topic of advice, not a requirement for consultation with state entities. Therefore, no outside party is involved in the decision-making process.

qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "State boating safety programs" and "principal advisor," which might imply consultation with states or external experts.
Resolution: The "principal advisor" is defined as "the individual with the highest rank who meets the experience qualifications," which refers to a senior Coast Guard officer (a federal employee). The reference to "State boating safety programs" is a subject matter over which the advisor provides advice to the Commandant, not a requirement to consult with state governments. All actors involved (Commandant, principal advisor, Coast Guard officers) are inside the federal government.
